    Salary. What is the salary of the Taoiseach of Ireland?
    About this result
    Feedback
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The Taoiseach of Ireland earns approximately €251,000 annually, a figure comprising a standard Teachta Dála (TD) salary of about €117,000 plus a ministerial allowance of roughly €134,000, though exact figures fluctuate slightly with pay adjustments. For instance, Micheál Martin's salary was reported as €251,261 as of August 2025, while Simon Harris's was around €239,089 in April 2024, showing recent changes. 
    Breakdown of the Salary
    • TD Base Salary: A standard TD's pay, currently around €117,113. 
    • Ministerial Allowance: An additional payment for holding the office of Taoiseach, roughly €134,148. 
    Key Details
    • Total Pay: The combination brings the total to roughly €251,261. 
    • Expenses: In addition to salary, the Taoiseach receives significant annual expenses, such as €134,148 as of August 2025. 
    • Variations: Salaries can change with public sector pay deals, with figures varying slightly by the date of the report.

      Role. What is the role of the Taoiseach of Ireland?
      Feedback
      The taoiseach is the head of government, or prime minister of Ireland. The office is appointed by the president of Ireland upon nomination by Dáil Éireann (the lower house of the Oireachtas, Ireland's national legislature) and the office-holder must retain the support of a majority in the Dáil to remain in office.

      Current Taoiseach. Who is the current Taoiseach of Ireland?
      About this result

      AI Overview
      The current Taoiseach (Prime Minister) of Ireland is Micheál Martin, leader of the Fianna Fáil party, who took office on January 23, 2025, following the 2024 general election and a coalition agreement. He previously served as Taoiseach from 2020 to 2022, then as Tánaiste (Deputy PM) before returning to the top job. 
      • Took office: January 23, 2025.
      • Political Party: Fianna Fáil.
      • Previous Role: Tánaiste (Dec 2022 - Jan 2025).

        Is Ireland still a free state?
        Following a national plebiscite in July 1937, the new Constitution of Ireland (Bunreacht na hÉireann) came into force on 29 December 1937. This replaced the Constitution of the Irish Free State and declared that the name of the state is Éire, or "Ireland" in the English language.

        What is the difference between an Irish president and a Taoiseach?
        The taoiseach (that is, Ireland's head of government) and ministers altogether comprise the Government, Ireland's central executive authority. The president formally appoints the members of the Government, and accepts their resignations.
